Sun Tzu was a Chinese general who, by tradition, wrote The Art of War, the most famous book on strategy ever written. He is said to have lived in the late 500s BCE, in the Eastern Zhou period, but his dates are traditional and his life is uncertain.

According to Sima Qian, writing four centuries later, he served King Helü of the southern state of Wu and led its armies to victory over the larger state of Chu. Many scholars think the book as we have it was written later, in the Warring States period, perhaps by several hands.

The book is short, in thirteen chapters. Its ideas are clear and memorable: know your enemy and know yourself; the best victory is won without fighting; all war is based on deception; use spies. A copy on bamboo strips found in a Han tomb at Yinqueshan in 1972 shows how old the text is. It has been read by Chinese and Japanese commanders, by Mao Zedong, and today by business leaders around the world.
